text: $agent-seat you are going to make a moped. The target poly count is ~2200 polygons. The goal here is to show your representation of a moped through your ability to reason about making it. you can use the image generator inside of the agent-skin skill which will let you generate reference images as many as you need to build from. The underlying goal is to create a detailed mesh and use the least amount of outliners as possible. You may find another existing moped, this is another models attempt at the same test. View it or not, I would say though its not what you want to take after.
resolution: Built and saved a detailed step-through moped directly in the live editor: 2,436 named resident triangles, 1.74 m measured bbox length by 1.09 m height with 0.50 m spoked wheels, four behavior-based Outliner rows (chassis, steering, front wheel, rear wheel), semantic regions for frame/body/engine/cockpit/wheels/details, a fitted 877x1010 atlas, and an oxblood workshop paint variant. Generated and used a temporary orthographic concept sheet, then removed the reference plane. Save and semantic-status report healthy with 2,436/2,436 named faces across saved, mount, and resident horizons and zero naming debt. No commit was created because repository instructions prohibit committing game 3D models.
